[EVIDENCE]  
- 42-year-old female — within typical age range for HD onset  
- 12-month duration of irritability and restlessness — recognized early behavioral features of HD  
- 12-month duration of auditory hallucinations — reported in prodromal and early HD cohorts  
- 1-month duration of dysphagia — documented early motor manifestation in HD, independent of overt chorea  
- Dysphagia occurs without hoarseness, neck swelling, or weight loss — reduces likelihood of structural or systemic malignancy or inflammation  
- Brain MRI shows atrophy of the caudate nuclei with ex vacuo dilatation of the frontal horns of the lateral ventricles — a hallmark neuroimaging feature of Huntington disease  

[GAPS]  
- Absence of documented motor signs (e.g., chorea, dystonia, bradykinesia) on neurological exam  
- Absence of oculomotor assessment (e.g., saccadic accuracy, pursuit)  
- Absence of cognitive testing results (e.g., executive function, verbal fluency)  
- Absence of family history of HD or unexplained neuropsychiatric/neurodegenerative illness  
- Absence of *HTT* gene CAG repeat count — definitive diagnostic test, pending  
- Absence of CSF analysis, serum autoantibodies, metabolic labs (e.g., ceruloplasmin, copper, B12, TSH), or whole-body imaging — all undetermined, not negative  

[DIAGNOSIS]  
Huntington disease
